newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine tells IMF complying with Article Eight.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine tells IMF complying with Article Eight.

text.p: Ukraine has told the International Monetary Fund that it has been complying with currency convertibility principles contained in the Article Eight of IMF charter, the Fund said in a press release faxed to Reuters on Tuesday.

"The Government of Ukraine has notified the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that it has accepted the obligations of Article VIII, Sections 2, 3, and 4, of the IMF Articles of Agreement, with effect from September 24, 1996," it said.

By accepting Article Eight, IMF members agree not to impose restrictions on payments and transfers for current account transactions -- essentially foreign trade -- and not to operate multiple currency regimes.
Accepting Article Eight is one of the conditions for Ukraine receiving a $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility loan, as is approval of this year's delayed budget.

Ukraine was giving "confidence to the international community that it will pursue sound economic policies that will obviate the need to use restrictions on the making of payments and transfers for current international transactions," the IMF press release said.
Convertibility under Article Eight would reduce the risk of investing or lending to Ukraine, making it easier to attract cheaper credits and investments.
President Leonid Kuchma is due to meet IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus when he visits Washington this week.
The national hryvnia currency is already convertible in Ukraine and on some interbank operations in Commonwealth of Independent States and Baltic states, but cannot otherwise be traded abroad.
